project_redefinition: A history of how microscopic knowledge was made durable, retrievable, movable, comparable and teachable through prepared objects and their documentary infrastructures, rather than a census or object history of glass slides alone.
core_proposition: The nineteenth-century microscope slide was a prepared, addressed and maintained knowledge object; material survival was only one form of continuity.
analytical_model: double fixing: preparation fixes material into a viewable state; address systems fix the preparation into recoverable relations. Both forms remain revisable and require maintenance.
working_conceptual_proposal: maintainable mobile: mobility and durability depend on material care, labels, packaging, catalogues, correspondence and repeated re-addressing rather than immutability of the glass carrier.
historiographical_guard: The project must not present slide materiality or slide circulation as discoveries in themselves. The repository already contains the 2013 HPLS slide literature by Löwy, Fiorentini, Gaycken and Close-Koenig. The distinctive moves are material publication, relation-bearing maintainability, asymmetric object/knowledge circulation, historically active address systems, commercial formatting, and comparative institutional coordination.

article_decision.first: Cole single-case article — Publishing the Preparation
article_decision.second: tight comparative article — Cole + Grunow + Pacini, with Quekett and Balfour as limit cases
article_decision.reason: Cole has the strongest bounded chronology and source density. Maintainability is the larger conceptual payoff but should be demonstrated through a tight comparative paper rather than a global typology.

Cole_article_moves: print/image/method compensate for the limits of the finished slide
cabinet and index materialize publication address
replacement and institutional separation reveal distributed publication identity
next_step: Draft the Cole article at first-order source density. State the historiographical intervention narrowly: not that slides are material/epistemic objects, but that Cole created a specific material publication technology whose serial and cabinet architecture made prepared objects issue-bound and historically durable across later material discontinuity.
